title: The Ambush and the Sikhs’ Last Stand Outside the Fort

blocks.text: Some Sikhs accepted the Mughal assurances and came out, but the enemy's show of respect could not be trusted. Once detachments were exposed beyond the fort, they found themselves surrounded from all sides and cut off from any orderly return.

The Singhs understood that retreat would not save them, so they chose to sacrifice their lives for the Guru's cause rather than die dishonored. They discharged the muskets they had already loaded, but soon could not reload their guns in the crush of battle.

After the first volleys, the fight closed into a fierce blood bath on the battlefield with swords, arrows, spears, and daggers. The page preserves the moment when the ambush turned into open martyrdom and the Sikhs answered treachery with direct combat.
